scope: Reviewed OMAI formula endpoints and exact Lean proof source for local theorems about derivatives of an atomistic or cell energy, with no Physlib physics counterpart. Hash and compiled-name checks detect drift and provenance errors; they are not automatic symbolic translation or numerical validation.
interpretations: E_tot is the total energy of the configuration as a differentiable function of all atomic Cartesian coordinates R_{i,alpha}; the catalog force F_{i,alpha} = -dE/dR_{i,alpha} is its exact partial derivative, the corrected total that codes report rather than the bare Hellmann-Feynman term.

Rigid translations shift every atom by the same vector. Invariance under them holds for an isolated system and for a periodic cell whose lattice translates with the atoms; real-space grids that break it (the egg-box effect) make the computed forces fail to sum to zero.

Rotations in a coordinate plane rotate every atom about the origin. Invariance under them holds for an isolated molecule or cluster, not for atoms rotated inside a fixed periodic lattice; the torque result applies only where it holds.

The cell energy is a function of the deformation gradient F = 1 + eps of the homogeneously strained cell, differentiable at F; V is the reference cell volume and sigma = -(1/V) dE/d eps is compressive positive, as the catalog states for QE. Invariance under rigid rotations of the deformed cell is objectivity of the energy.

compute_fc2_finite_displacement is the exact derivative -dF_j/du_i; the finite_displacement scheme estimates it by central differences (F(u - h e_i) - F(u + h e_i))/(2h). When a site symmetry maps the plus displacement onto the minus one, phonopy reconstructs the minus forces by symmetry and the estimate stays the central difference; a truly one-sided difference has an error of order h. Neither case is covered.
